title: Turn scores into a loss, then check the gradients of a whole network
brief: Write a stable softmax and cross-entropy whose slope is prediction minus truth, wire the engine into a two-layer network, and write the finite-difference check that proves its gradients.
hints: softmax: subtract each row's maximum with keepdims=True, exponentiate, then divide by the row sum. The shift changes no probability and keeps exp from overflowing.
log_softmax: (z - m) - log(sum(exp(z - m))) for the same shift m. Do not take log of softmax(z), because small probabilities underflow to 0.

In softmax_cross_entropy, pick each row's correct entry with log_probs[np.arange(n), labels]. The slope on the logits is (softmax(z) - one_hot(labels)) / n: subtract 1 at the correct entry of each row, then divide by n because the loss is a mean.

mlp_loss_and_grad: wrap every W and b in a fresh Tensor, compute h @ W + b for each layer, apply .relu() on every layer except the last, call softmax_cross_entropy on the last output, call backward() once, then copy each .grad.
numeric_grad: copy the array, and for each entry (np.ndindex helps) nudge it up by h, measure the loss, nudge it down by h, measure the loss, restore it, and record (high - low) / (2h).

gradient_check: for each parameter array, compare the analytic gradient with numeric_grad. Use norm(analytic - numeric) / (norm(analytic) + norm(numeric)), and return the largest value over all arrays. Inside the loss function, build a new params list with only that one array replaced.
